summary: Duplicate Okta email alias prevents session cookie issuance for internal Model Hub behind auth-proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Users who had an Okta profile migration earlier this week (secondary email alias added) are unable to obtain a session cookie when accessing Model Hub (internal model catalog) behind the nginx auth-proxy. The request completes through Okta SSO and returns HTTP 200 to the proxy, but the proxy's response does not include the session cookie (session_id) and the browser ends up on the login page in a loop.

Impact:
- ~12 users in Data Science and Platform reported inability to use Model Hub; affects internal workflows for model review and artifact uploads.
- Not a broad outage but blocks those users' day-to-day tasks.

Environment:
- Prod environment, us-east region, Model Hub served behind nginx auth-proxy and internal console edge. Okta tenant: redwood-prod.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Okta session created in browser via primary login (okta.com redirect flow).
2) User gets redirected back to auth-proxy with SAML/OIDC assertion.
3) Auth-proxy responds 200 but Set-Cookie: session_id header is missing.
4) Browser performs an extra redirect to /login; no session persistence.

Expected behavior:
- After SSO flow succeds, auth-proxy should issue session cookie scoped to .internal.redwood and Model Hub should receive authenticated session.

Observed behavior:
- Auth-proxy treats the request as unauthenticated because cookie issuance path is skipped when Okta profile contains secondaryEmail attribute (duplicate email aliases) and the proxy header mapping logic returns an array causing header serialization to break.

Relevant logs / links:
- Sentry errors aggregated under project: console-auth (see event stream): https://sentry.redwood.com/console-auth/issues/?query=session_cookie
- Grafana auth-proxy dashboard spike for Set-Cookie failure rate: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/auth-proxy
- Okta system logs show successful assertion for the affected users: https://dashboard.okta.com/admin/apps/okta/events (internal link)
steps_to_reproduce: Login to Okta with account that has secondary email alias
Complete redirect back to auth-proxy for Model Hub
Observe network trace: missing Set-Cookie header on auth-proxy response
Browser redirected back to /login without session cookie
comments: 2026-03-10 10:15 - Liam O'Connor (support): Confirmed 3 reproducible cases from DS team; captured HAR files and shared via #support-auth channel

2026-03-10 11:02 - Priya Shah (oncall-auth): Reproduced locally with a user profile that has secondaryEmail set; proxy returned 200 but no Set-Cookie. Added more verbose logging to auth-proxy in staging.

2026-03-11 09:47 - SRE (Marta Ruiz): Trace shows header 'x-okta-email' being populated as a JSON array for migrated profiles; nginx header map expected string and silently dropped Set-Cookie generation path.
2026-03-12 14:30 - Priya Shah: Deployed a quick patch in staging to coerce header to string and verified cookie issuance. Planning controlled prod roll out after code review. See PR in repo.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Aisha Patel: Informed affected users of workaround (use incognito + login then open Model Hub) while we roll out fix.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: cookie issuance conditional branch depends on sanitized email header; secondaryEmail array breaks truthy check.
Captured request/response via HAR from affected user: Okta assert -> auth-proxy 200 -> response headers missing Set-Cookie; upstream session-store logs show no session create call.

Added debug logs to auth-proxy; found code path that sets 'user_email' from request header 'x-okta-email'. When header contained '["user@company.com", "alt@company.com"]' the string check failed and function returned before session creation.
Reviewed Okta migration job; it writes a 'secondaryEmail' attribute for legacy profiles and our Okta-to-proxy transform had a regression where it serialized arrays for headers.
Staging test with a coerced header (first element) results in correct Set-Cookie; suggests fix is safe to apply with feature flag and targeted rollout.
Cross-referenced similar tickets: INT-614824 (email-alias), but that ticket was SCIM-sync related and different failure mode (orphaned approval queues).
resolution: Deployed auth-proxy patch that normalizes x-okta-email header to a single primary value if an array is detected (feature-flagged).
Rolled out to prod (us-east) in a canary cohort of 10% at 2026-03-12 15:00; monitored Set-Cookie issuance and user logins. Success: set-cookie rate returned to baseline within 20 minutes.
Full rollout completed by 2026-03-12 16:45. Affected users confirmed they can access Model Hub without workarounds.

Follow-ups: (1) Work with Okta provisioning team to avoid array serialization in headers; (2) Add unit tests for header normalization path; (3) Update runbook to include this class of failure and a diagnostic script.
